hints: Count the conducting area in the cross-section diagram: one thick strand of area $4A$ plus eight thin strands each of area $A$, all of length $L$ in parallel.
Recall that parallel wires of the same material and length act like one wire whose area is the sum of the separate areas, and that $R = \rho L / A_{total}$.
Rearrange to $\rho = R A_{total} / L$ and substitute $A_{total} = 4A + 8 \times A$ to find the numerator.
walkthrough: Identify the parallel combination: all nine copper strands have the same length $L$ and same p.d., so their conductances add. For equal $\rho$ and $L$, this is equivalent to adding areas.
Calculate the total effective cross-sectional area: $A_{total} = 4A + 8 \times A = 12A$.
State the resistivity rule for a uniform conductor: $R = \rho L / A_{total}$ where $R$ is the measured total cable resistance.
Rearrange for resistivity: multiply by $A_{total}$ and divide by $L$ to get $\rho = R A_{total} / L$.
Substitute $A_{total} = 12A$: $\rho = 12AR/L$, with units $\Omega \text{m}$. This is option D.

options.A: This inverts $R$ and $L$ and has units of $\text{m}^{-1} \Omega^{-1}$, not resistivity, so it cannot be $\rho = RA/L$.
options.B: This has $R$ and $L$ in the denominator, giving units of $\Omega^{-1} \text{m}^{-1}$, which is not the unit of resistivity.
options.C: This uses only the thick strand area $4A$ and omits the $8A$ contributed by the eight thin strands in parallel.
options.D: With total parallel area $4A + 8A = 12A$, $\rho = R \times 12A / L$, which has correct units of $\Omega \text{m}$.
